//: reflection hook data — quality warnings to raise about the code just written (language- and team-specific).
//engine: The engine (core) hardcodes no language rules. Only the generic TODO/FIXME rule is built in; everything else is data here.
//format: glob=file to apply to, globs=array of file patterns (omit both to apply to everything), regex=Python re pattern, enabled=false disables the rule, min_count=fire only at this many matches or more (default 1), message={count} is replaced with the match count
//packs: packs are opt-in rule bundles. In a project that wants one, flip that pack's enabled to true.
//builtins: To turn the built-in TODO/FIXME warning off: "builtins": {"todo_fixme": false}
//example: rules are enabled-by-default Kotlin examples; packs are disabled-by-default opt-in examples. Adapt them to your language and rules.

rules.message: {count} use(s) of `!!` — consider replacing with requireNotNull or ?: return

packs.name: react-async-timing
packs.description: Candidates for React effect and async ordering risks. These are regex warnings, so check the real scope and execution order.

rules.message: {count} candidate side effect(s) inside a state updater — an updater can re-run, so consider moving localStorage/save/fetch to an effect or event boundary. tsc and existing tests do not guarantee ordering, so reproduce it with renderHook + rerender
{count} candidate catch path(s) with no loaded/ready/settled completion signal — check that later saves are not blocked forever. Reproduce the pending->reject order with renderHook + rerender

{count} candidate render path(s) branching on ref.current — changing a ref does not trigger a rerender. Check whether this is render scope, and consider moving to state or a derived value plus a rerender test

{count} candidate effect(s) whose first action resets a state collection — check whether it overwrites a value filled in by a parent or another effect in the same commit. Test the mount, account switch, and unmount-then-remount order
